messages:
Ava: Quick heads-up — planning a small canary for model v2.3-int4-slim across a split A/B on two synthetic slices at 03:30 PT. Need final gating params before we open traffic.

Jon: OK, can you paste the draft gating config here?

Ava: Draft below — wanting automated fallback if quality delta or latency tail regresses. Open to tightening.
```json
{
  \"canary_percent\": 5,
  \"windows\": { \"eval_window_minutes\": 15, \"check_interval_minutes\": 5 },
  \"metrics\": {
    \"composite_delta_threshold\": 0.07,
    \"token_kl_threshold\": 0.05,
    \"p99_latency_multiplier\": 1.6,
    \"min_samples\": 800,
    \"consecutive_fail_windows\": 2
  },
  \"cohort_weights\": { \"enterprise\": 0.6, \"consumer\": 0.4 },
  \"auto_fallback\": { \"action\": \"route-to-stable\", \"notify\": [\"#incidents\", \"@oncall\"] }
}
```

Priya: What exactly is \"composite_delta\" here? Is that the same formula we used in last promo?

Ava: Slight variant — composite = 0.5 * (1 - normalized_embedding_cosine) + 0.3 * normalized_response_length_diff + 0.2 * token_KL. Normalizations are z-scored against a rolling baseline. It weights semantic drift > brevity changes.

eval-bot: Shadow run summary (30m): composite_delta=0.038, token_KL=0.021, p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=180ms. Baseline p99=110ms. Sample_count=1,220. No top-level regressions detected.

Devin: p99 looks concerning (180 vs 110). I know we give some headroom but tail could still trigger noisy fallbacks. Suggest p99_multiplier=1.5 and increase consecutive_fail_windows to 3. Also bump min_samples to 1,000.

Ava: Good call. I can tighten p99 to 1.5 and min_samples=1000. That will reduce false positives from sparse noise.

Jon: Are we going to weight any business-critical slices higher at runtime? e.g., searches vs assistant?

Ava: Yes — cohort_weights already reflect that. For this canary we treat the enterprise search slice as 60% of the composite scoring. Means a regression there matters more.

Priya: Can we add a short-circuit: if token_KL > 0.08 in any window, immediate fallback?

Ava: Agree. Adding immediate KL short-circuit.

Ava: Updated config snippet:
```json
{
  \"canary_percent\": 5,
  \"metrics\": {\n    \"composite_delta_threshold\": 0.07,\n    \"token_kl_threshold\": 0.05,\n    \"token_kl_immediate\": 0.08,\n    \"p99_latency_multiplier\": 1.5,\n    \"min_samples\": 1000,\n    \"consecutive_fail_windows\": 3\n  },
  \"auto_fallback\": { \"action\": \"route-to-stable\" }
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled and kicked off at 03:30 PT. API call: `POST /rollout/start {model: \"v2.3-int4-slim\", canary:5, slices:[\"enterprise-search\",\"longform\"]}` :rocket:

Devin: I'll watch the telemetry dashboard (link) and sample failing requests. If we see oscillation we should pause and widen the eval_window.

Jon: Also add a short test that confirms prefix-KV warmup matches stable model for top queries — otherwise latency comparisons are noisy.

Ava: Good reminder. Added warmup check: require at least 3 successful prefix warms in the first 10m or hold canary.

eval-bot: Early 10m check passed. Warmup_ok=true. Composite rolling=0.029, p99_multiplier=1.64 (slightly above tightened 1.5) — monitoring.

Priya: If p99 stays above 1.5 but composite still low, do we still fallback? We should avoid failing on latency alone for short spikes.

Ava: The rule is: if p99 > multiplier for 3 consecutive windows OR composite_delta > threshold for 1 window, trigger fallback. KL immediate triggers immediate fallback. That balances quality-first with tail sensitivity.

Devin: Sounds reasonable. I'll add a small alert runbook for ops if fallback triggers: steps to reproduce and where to pull sample traces.

Ava: Thanks — action items: 1) deploy config with p99_multiplier=1.5 & token_kl_immediate=0.08 (done), 2) Devin to monitor and triage, 3) Priya to run targeted embed concordance tests post-canary.

Jon: :thumbsup: good to go.

deploy-bot: Canary live (5%). Monitoring channels: #eng-ml, #infra-observe.

Ava: Closing loop — please paste any anomalies here. If fallback happens, we'll capture samples and open a postmortem template.
